title: How to connect Scispot's MCP server to your AI tools
summary: Step-by-step guide to connecting Scispot's MCP server to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Claude Code and VS Code, so you can work with your lab data in plain language.
body_markdown:
Scispot's MCP server lets an AI assistant work with your Scispot workspace. You can ask questions in plain language, look up lab data, and, if you choose, have the assistant make supported changes.


This guide shows how to connect Scispot to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Claude Code and VS Code (GitHub Copilot).


MCP access is included at no additional cost with an active Scispot subscription. Use of the MCP server is subject to your Scispot agreement and Scispot's[Terms of Use](https://www.scispot.com/legal/terms-of-use) , and its features and availability may change over time.


**Server address (you'll need this in every section):**


```text
https://mcp.scispot.io/
```


## Before you start


**1. A Scispot account with the right access.**


- You need a Scispot Super Admin account, or an account with both Dry Lab and MCP access. If you're not sure which you have, ask your Scispot admin.
- Your Scispot admin must add you to Scispot before you connect.
- You sign in with your own Scispot account (Microsoft SSO or a magic link, per Scispot's docs). Nobody shares a login.


**2. An AI tool that supports custom connectors.** Adding a custom connector in ChatGPT requires a workspace admin or owner. For Claude, Cursor, Claude Code and VS Code, see each provider's own MCP documentation for what your account needs.


Permissions and menus are set by each provider and change often. Check the provider's current help pages.


**3. Your organization's approval.** You are connecting an AI tool to lab data. Check your organization's data-handling and approval rules first. Scispot's docs recommend OAuth sign-in over API tokens.


## Important note on how to use this connector


Scispot's MCP server is for research and laboratory data workflows. It is not designed for, and must not be used for, protected health information (PHI) as defined under HIPAA or other individually identifiable health information. Don't use the MCP server, or any AI tool connected to it, to send, store, process or retrieve PHI. Scispot doesn't authorize these integrations for healthcare services, clinical care, clinical decision support, or any workflow involving PHI.


The connector acts with the permissions of the connected Scispot account. When you use it through an AI tool, your use is also subject to that AI provider's own terms and privacy policy. See Scispot's[Privacy Policy](https://www.scispot.com/privacy-policy) and[Terms of Use](https://www.scispot.com/legal/terms-of-use) .


## Connect to ChatGPT (as a custom connector)


Scispot isn't available in ChatGPT's app directory. To use it with ChatGPT, you add it yourself as a custom MCP server.


**Who can do this:** a workspace admin or owner. If you aren't one, ask yours to do steps 1 to 7. An admin then publishes it to the workspace. Per OpenAI, you don't need to turn on Developer Mode in the current Plugins experience.


1. In ChatGPT, go to **Plugins** .
2. Select the **+** button, then **Add custom MCP server** .
3. Enter a name (for example "Scispot") and, if you like, a description.
4. Under **Connection** , enter the server address:` https://mcp.scispot.io/`
5. Configure authentication for the server and choose OAuth.
6. Read the risk warning, tick **I understand and want to continue** , then select **Create as a plugin** . Review the tools ChatGPT discovers.
7. Sign in with your Scispot account when asked and approve.
8. Start a new chat, type **@** , pick Scispot, and try a read-only prompt (see "Prompts to try" below).


**Good to know**


- ChatGPT may ask you to confirm before it takes an action. Read the request before approving.
- After an admin publishes the connector, ChatGPT uses a saved snapshot of its tools. If tools change later, an admin may need to refresh the tool list.
- Deep research can use custom connectors for reading only, not writing.


## Connect to Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)


Custom connectors are set up in your Claude account, so the steps are the same on claude.ai and Claude Desktop.


**Adding the connector yourself:**


1. Go to **Customize > Connectors** .
2. Select **+ Add** , then **Add custom connector** .
3. Name it "Scispot" and enter` https://mcp.scispot.io/` . Select **Continue** .
4. Under Authentication, choose **Sign in now** (or "Sign in when needed"). Leave the OAuth client on the recommended option.
5. Select **Add** , then **Connect** . Sign in to Scispot, select your workspace and review the permissions, as described in Scispot's docs.
6. In a chat, use the **+** button, then **Connectors** , and turn Scispot on.


**If your organization manages connectors in Claude:** an Owner or admin goes to **Organization settings > Connectors > Add > Custom > Web** , enters the name and server address, and finishes the setup. Each person then goes to **Customize > Connectors** , finds Scispot and selects **Connect** . If you don't see the option, ask your Claude admin.


## Connect to Cursor


1. Open your` mcp.json` (Cursor also lets you manage MCP servers from its **Customize** page).
2. Add Scispot as a remote server:


```text
{
"mcpServers": {
"scispot": {
"url": "https://mcp.scispot.io/"
}
}
}
```


1. Cursor supports OAuth for remote servers. When it connects, sign in with your Scispot account.
2. In chat, ask a read-only question to test.


If sign-in doesn't work, open the Output panel, choose **MCP Logs** , and check for errors.


## Connect to Claude Code


1. In your terminal, run:


```text
claude mcp add --transport http scispot-mcp https://mcp.scispot.io/
```


1. Start Claude Code with` claude` , then type` /mcp` .
2. Find` scispot-mcp` . It should show **Needs Authorization** . Select it and choose **Authenticate** .
3. Sign in to Scispot in your browser, select your workspace and permissions, and finish.
4. Back in Claude Code, ask: "List my Scispot Labsheets."


If sign-in later expires, open` /mcp` and re-authenticate the server.


## Connect to VS Code (GitHub Copilot)


1. In VS Code, with Copilot selected, run **Chat: Open Customizations** from the Command Palette and select **MCP Servers** .
2. Select **Add Server (+)** , choose **HTTP** , and enter` https://mcp.scispot.io/` .
3. Give it a server ID such as` scispot` , and choose where to save it.
4. Review any trust requests and follow any sign-in steps that appear.
5. Test with a low-impact, read-only request, and expand the tool call to confirm it used Scispot.


## Any other AI tool


Per Scispot's docs, any client that supports remote HTTP MCP servers can be used: add a remote MCP server, set the connection URL to` https://mcp.scispot.io/` , choose OAuth, sign in with your Scispot account, and confirm with a read-only request before you do anything that changes data. If your client can't complete the sign-in, see Troubleshooting.


## Prompts to try


Start with read-only requests:


1. "List my Scispot Labsheets."
2. "Show the schema of the 'Cell Lines' Labsheet, then find rows where Status is 'Active'."
3. "List the protocols in the 'Genomics' Labspace and summarize the 'DNA Extraction SOP' protocol."
4. "Look up the manifest with barcode 'PLT-00142' and show which wells are filled."


Swap in the names of your own Labsheets, Labspaces and barcodes. Use research and lab data only. No PHI or other individually identifiable health information.


## Making changes safely


The connector can also create and update records (such as Labsheet rows and ELN pages), acting with the permissions of the connected Scispot account. Start with read-only requests.


AI tools can misread requests or make mistakes, and changes made through the connector are real changes to your Scispot data that may not be easy to undo. Whether your AI tool asks you to confirm an action depends on that tool and its settings, so don't rely on a confirmation prompt.


Review the data and the planned action before you approve any change. For important records, ask the AI to summarize the proposed changes first, then check the record in Scispot afterwards. Some tools overwrite existing rows or page content, so take extra care with those.


## Troubleshooting


- **You can't add the connector.** Check that you entered the server address exactly as shown above. In ChatGPT you need a workspace admin or owner, and your Claude organization may require an admin.
- **Sign-in fails or loops.** Make sure your Scispot admin has added you, and that you're using your own Scispot account (Microsoft SSO or magic link). If it still fails, contact Scispot Customer Support at cs@scispot.io.
- **You need to reconnect.** Claude: **Customize > Connectors** , then disconnect and connect again. Claude Code:` /mcp` , then re-authenticate. ChatGPT: **Settings > Plugins** , then select Scispot to manage or reconnect. Cursor: check MCP Logs and re-add the server if needed.
- **You can't see data or an action fails.** The connector acts with your Scispot account's permissions. Check that you can do the same action in Scispot with the same account, and ask your admin to review your role if not.
- **The AI proposes an unexpected change.** Don't approve it. Ask it to explain, then check the records in Scispot.
